name: Time Machine check plugin
summary: an optional plugin, off until you switch it on, that checks every 15 minutes that Apple's Time Machine made a backup in the last 24 hours and raises one alert when it did not or cannot tell. A computer with no Time Machine disk set up gets no alert.
description: The time machine check plugin runs tmutil once every 15 minutes (first pass a minute after it starts), off the event loop, and keeps one alert. A backup older than 24 hours raises it at once; a read that fails raises a cannot-tell alert on the second pass in a row, with a check access explainer that opens the Full Disk Access setting; a backup running right now changes nothing; a healthy backup, or a computer with no Time Machine destination, closes the alert. Its re-check now button posts to the plugin's own route. It ships off for everyone and needs only the notify permission.
where: The plugins page: the time machine check switch (link: #plugins). Its alert appears in the alert center with a re-check now button.
how_to: Open the plugins page and switch on the time machine check; macOS asks nothing, but reading the newest backup needs Full Disk Access for Carnivore, and the cannot-tell alert's check access button opens that setting.
Press re-check now on the alert, or POST /api/v1/cplugs/timemachine/check, to run a pass at once.
examples: A laptop away from its backup disk for two days gets the stale alert.
A new install without Full Disk Access gets the cannot-tell alert with the steps.
A computer that never set up Time Machine gets nothing.
media_exempt: no screen of its own: a switch drawn by the generic plugins page and an alert drawn by the existing alert panel, so there is nothing new to capture
